dimensions.assessment: Involves regional water system entities, federal agencies, and prospective municipal, rural, and industrial water users across four states.
dimensions.evidence: supply municipal, rural, and industrial water to the Dakota Mainstem Regional Water System service area in the States of South Dakota, Iowa, Nebraska, and Minnesota

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes a study and reporting process rather than immediate project construction.
dimensions.evidence: carry out a study to determine the feasibility of constructing the Dakota Mainstem Water Supply Project

dimensions.assessment: Limits federal expenditures for the study to a maximum of $10,000,000 with a 50 percent federal cost share.
dimensions.evidence: Not more than $10,000,000 of Federal funds may be expended to carry out the feasibility study under this section.

dimensions.assessment: Directs a specific feasibility study and report to congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: develop a feasibility report that includes a recommendation of the Secretary

dimensions.assessment: Temporary study authority expiring five years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The authority provided by this section expires on the date that is 5 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Total estimated cost of eventual project construction if found feasible
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a feasibility study for a regional water supply project in South Dakota, Iowa, Nebraska, and Minnesota, with a federal funding cap of $10 million.
